get.description:
Streams one file with the captures that match the filters, oldest first. Needs the viewer role. Bearer tokens are refused (`session_required`); a view-protected anonymous endpoint needs `X-Webhooks-Live-Grant`.

Formats: `json` is one document with `format`, `version`, `exported_at`, `endpoint` and `captures`; `ndjson` is the same header on the first line, then one capture per line; `csv` is a header row, then one row per capture (no endpoint); `zip` holds `captures.ndjson` (every capture, without bodies) and `bodies/<seq>-<capture id>.bin` for every capture with a stored body. A capture whose stored body is missing is left out of json, ndjson and csv.

Filters are the capture list filters: `method`, `status`, `kind`, `starred`, `q`, `after_seq`, `since` and `until`; `order`, `limit` and `cursor` are ignored. `format` is required.

The selection is measured before the first byte: above the tier's export size the answer is 422 `export_too_large`. Once streaming has started, a failure ends the body early: a client that reads nothing for 30 seconds, output above twice the tier size, or a run longer than 10 minutes. The client must treat a body that stops before its end as failed. Quota: `exports` per hour (`quota_exceeded`, `error.limit.name` = `exports`; by default 10 per endpoint for anonymous callers and 30 per user for signed-in callers). One export at a time per caller, and 2 per replica by default (`EXPORT_CONCURRENCY`): an export over either limit answers 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After: 1`.

post.description:
Needs a session; a token is refused (`session_required`). The caller needs the editor role on an owned endpoint; an unowned endpoint in `mixed` answers 409 `claim_required`. The body is the JSON document or the NDJSON file of `GET /endpoints/{id}/export`, sent as `Content-Type: application/json` or `application/x-ndjson` (parameters after `;` are ignored). Other types answer 415 before the body is read. The header must carry `format` = `webhooks-live-export`, `version` = 1, `exported_at` and `endpoint`. Response: `imported`, `skipped` and `reason`, which is `capacity`, `storage` or null when everything was imported.

A declared `Content-Length` above the tier's import size answers 413 before the body is read, and a stream above it stops with 413. The upload must keep sending: 30 seconds without data, or a run longer than 10 minutes, answers 400 `invalid_json`. `keep_times` (default `true`): with `true` each capture keeps its `received_at`, which must lie between 2015-01-01 and five minutes after now; with `false` each capture gets the import time; any other value answers 422. The first problem stops the import with 422 `validation_failed`, `field` = `captures.<index>.<path>` (JSON) or `line.<n>` (NDJSON); the captures stored before it stay. Once the endpoint is full or the storage limit is reached, the rest is counted as `skipped` and `reason` names the cause.

Limits: one import at a time per caller and 2 per replica (429 `rate_limited`, `Retry-After: 1`); a user whose import has finished waits 60 seconds before the next one (429 `rate_limited`, `Retry-After` set); the `imports` quota per day (429 `quota_exceeded`, `error.limit.name` = `imports`; by default 10 per user).

post.description:
Sends the request and answers the response in the same call. In `open` and `mixed` anyone may send; in `sso` a session is needed. A token needs the `send` scope. The composer must be on, else 404 `not_found`.

`method` is GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or OPTIONS, in any case. `url` is an absolute `http` or `https` URL without user information, at most 2048 bytes. A `body` is `{encoding, data}`: `encoding` is `utf8` or `base64`, and the decoded body is at most 1 MiB. A capture URL of this instance (`/<endpoint id>/...` on the public host) is delivered inside the instance and `capture_id` names the capture; other URLs of this instance are refused. Private and reserved addresses are refused unless the operator's forward allow list covers them.

A delivery that fails is still 200: `status` is null and `error` is `<code>: <detail>`, with the codes `timeout`, `refused_target`, `refused_redirect`, `dns_failure`, `connect_timeout`, `hop_timeout`, `total_timeout`, `too_many_redirects`, `transport`, `configuration` and `local_delivery`. `timeout_ms` defaults to 15000 and may not exceed it. Redirects are followed only with `follow_redirects: true`, at most 5. `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection` and the other hop-by-hop headers, `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Client-IP`, `True-Client-IP`, `CF-Connecting-IP`, and any name starting with `Proxy-` or `X-Webhooks-Live-` answer 422 `not_allowed`.

Each send is charged to the `outbound` quota: a signed-in caller per hour, an anonymous caller per network per day and, with `endpoint_id`, per endpoint per hour. A request that arrives with `X-Webhooks-Live-Hop` of 3 or more answers 422 `hop_limit`; each delivery carries the next count, so loops through the instance stop. A send by a signed-in caller, and an anonymous send with `endpoint_id`, is kept in the history.

Or `hop_limit`
